newsitem.title: GERMANY: Police detain couple in online child sex case.
newsitem.headline: Police detain couple in online child sex case.

text.p: German police said on Friday they had detained a man and a woman accused of using an online service to offer children for sado-masochistic sex, culminating in the death of the victims.

The 30-year old haulage contracter and his 36-year old girlfriend from the Bavarian town of Rosenheim offered children to users of the computerised chat service to perform "sadistic acts without limits", police said.
The couple, who were detained earlier this week at their home, told police they had not been serious about the offers and had made them purely to fuel their sexual fantasies.

The couple, using the cover names "Domina the Leather Witch" and "Sado-Hangman", offered foreign children for sex for 12,000 marks (around $7,400) and said if a child died they would dispose of the body for a further 15,000 marks ($9,200).
Deutsche Telekom, which runs the T-Online service used by the couple, said it could never make its system completely "clean" but urged users to report any offensive material they came across.

Germany has been active in its efforts to stamp out the use of online services and the global Internet computer network for distribution of pornographic images, especially those using children, as well as text from extremist political groups.

At the end of 1995, German authorities forced the online service CompuServe to shut down access to more than 200 Internet news groups because it suspected they were used to distribute child pornography, which is illegal in Germany.
